title: Creature Vocal Forge: Monster Voice Sound Effects
shortText: 120 monster voice SFX: 12 creatures, each with idle loop, alert, attack, hurt, death and a special. WAV + OGG.
html:
12 monsters, every one a whole voice set

120 creature voice sound effects. 12 creatures, and every one ships the same 6 states: idle, alert, attack, hurt, death, special.

Wiring one enemy usually means an idle from one pack, an attack from another and a death from a third, and the creature stops sounding like one animal. Here every creature is one synthesised throat, and every state it needs comes out of that same throat. Your state machine maps one state to one file name for the whole bestiary.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. A plain language licence ships in the zip, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. The one thing you may not do is resell the sounds as a sound pack. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 30 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. Two whole creatures (the dire wolf and the goblin, every state and every take) and the alert call of every other creature in the pack.

The bestiary

  • Ogre: A huge chest and a slow temper: low bellows with a rough edge. Special: roar.
  • Stone Golem: No lungs, only stone: a grinding groan with rock in every joint. Special: rockslide.
  • Marsh Toad Brute: A bloated throat that croaks in pulses and gulps wet air. Special: tongue lash.
  • Bog Slime: Not a throat at all: a body that gurgles, bubbles and splits. Special: split.
  • Ghoul: A dead throat dragging air: rasping, breathy, teeth clicking. Special: feast.
  • Dire Wolf: A predator: snarls, yelps and one long howl. Special: howl.
  • Goblin: Small, quick and nasal: gibbering, squealing, cackling. Special: cackle.
  • Wyvern: A winged reptile: bright screeches with a rasp underneath. Special: dive screech.
  • Wraith: A cold, airy voice with no body behind it: wails and whispers. Special: keen.
  • Giant Spider: Almost voiceless: hissing, and mandibles that click. Special: web spit.
  • Grave Rat: Tiny and many: squeaks and chattering teeth. Special: swarm.
  • Cave Bat: The smallest throat here: chirps, clicks and leathery wings. Special: echolocation.

Every creature, the same states

  • idle: a seamless loop of breathing and the odd soft call, at that creature's own breathing rate
  • alert (2 takes), attack (2 takes) and hurt (3 takes), so the same cry never has to play twice in a row
  • death and a signature special

Checked from the shipped files, not promised: every creature carries all 6 states, the 180 pairs of states inside each creature all differ, and the 66 pairs of creatures all differ in brightness or length, so the cast is 12 voices and not one growl played at 12 pitches.

In the box

  • 120 sounds in .wav (16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono) and .ogg
  • 12 seamless idle loops with loop points written into the files (smpl chunk and OGG loop tags)
  • 36 variation sets for anti repetition
  • One loudness across the pack: the inner 80 percent of files sit inside 0.29 dB, so a rat and an ogre play at the same level
  • A naming manifest, per engine import notes (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker, Web) and a proof file with a sha256 and a measurement record for every sound

Honest limits

These are synthesised voices, not recorded actors or animals. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. No footsteps, no weapons, no music and no human speech.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover art and store graphics are AI generated.

More from the same studio

  • Steel and Bone, medieval combat impacts: the weapon hits that land on these creatures.
  • Portcullis, dungeon mechanisms: the doors, chests, levers and traps of the lairs they live in.
  • Sixfold, elemental casting chains: the spells your party throws back at them.
